A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynthAgent study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, synthetic-data quality measurements, component ablations and data-scaling results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and analysis results and adds Qwen3-VL-8B evaluations in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Categorized exploration, conflict-triggered task refinement, offline trajectory editing and supervised fine-tuning are unchanged. Expanded explanations of conservative editing introduce no new operation; all six appendix prompts retain identical content.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five WebArena environments and Online-Mind2Web coverage. Qwen3 experiments reuse these benchmarks; the newly discussed Mind2Web and WebShop limitations do not represent additional evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 adds untuned Qwen3-VL-8B as the reference comparator for its SynthAgent-trained counterpart in Tables 3–4. Comparator membership in the existing experiments, including Self-Instruct, OS-Genesis and Explorer, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds the Qwen3-VL-8B configuration using the same SynthAgent-generated training data. Existing evaluation samples, metrics, 30-step budget and stated fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Qwen3 experiments add a limited check of whether the same synthetic supervision remains useful with a stronger backbone. Existing component ablations, scaling curves, judge comparisons, refinement analyses and case studies are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and the same averaging across judges. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Tables 3–4 report Qwen3 base versus SynthAgent success rates of 15.93 versus 24.34 on WebArena and judge averages of 18.67 versus 24.11 on Online-Mind2Web. These are additional backbone results; all matched pre-existing numerical tables and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, conflict predicate in Equation 1 and supervised objective in Equation 2 are retained. Added conceptual explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain fully synthetic adaptation through categorized exploration and dual refinement, with improved data quality and agent performance. The rewritten third contribution emphasizes benefits already claimed in v2; the abstract and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive limitations section covering interactive-environment requirements, live-site synthesis obstacles, GPT-4.1 dependence, untuned execution parameters and SFT-only training. Section 4.2 also interprets smaller Qwen3 gains as possibly reflecting capabilities already present in stronger models and acknowledges modest absolute success rates.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the added Qwen3-VL-8B configuration and reuse of the existing synthetic data, and newly discloses the absence of synthesis/execution hyperparameter tuning. Existing implementation instructions, prompts and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Qwen3-VL, OpenCUA and Direct Preference Optimization. Section 2.3 positions OpenCUA’s richer human-annotated supervision as complementary future work; positioning against the principal synthesis methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds SynthAgent to the title, revises selected introduction and method paragraphs, incorporates two appendix analyses into the main narrative, and adds Limitations, Ethics Statement and Use of AI Assistants sections. Most existing prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two Qwen3 result tables and moves existing exploration/refinement Tables 7–9 into the main analysis. It reformats the action table and some prompt boxes and resolves duplicated table numbering. The six figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone evidence strengthens support for reuse of the synthetic data, while explicit limitations and clearer method explanations improve transparency. These are limited gains over otherwise stable evidence. A new weakness is the Ethics Statement’s claim that research occurred entirely in self-hosted environments, which conflicts with the retained live-site evaluation.
